newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain employers abandon key demand in labour talks.
newsitem.headline: Spain employers abandon key demand in labour talks.

text.p: Spain's employers have abandoned their demands for lower dismissal costs which have proved to be the key sticking point in labour talks so far, a union spokesman said on Wednesday.
Employers and unions returned to the negotiating table on Wednesday in an attempt to reach an accord on crucial labour reforms after intensive talks on Tuesday failed to result in a deal.
"Employers have abandoned their demands for lower severance pay," a union representative told reporters.
Without explicitly confirming or denying this possibility, employer representatives said it was "plausible".

Employers have been demanding an expansion of current dismissal regulations that would effectively cut costs to employers. In the event of redundancies, employers also do not want to have to justify cases before a judge.
"We must have a more flexible wording," a source from employers' association CEOE told Reuters.
Participants in the negotiations have hinted that a large part of Wednesday's talks would be absorbed in drawing up new contracts to stimulate jobs for youths.
